title: MAC a link that pads differently

blocks.text: We are joining a regional debit network. Its MAC is the retail MAC, but its specification pads the MAC input differently from the links we had so far. The relevant section is copied into the class comment of `src/main/java/com/example/practice/NetworkMac.java`.

In the network's test window, some of our messages were refused as wrongly MACed, and their security team asked how our side treats the MACs it receives: their test script sends answers with a MAC that is wrong, shortened or missing, and expects every one of them to be refused.
`mac` already runs the algorithm; it calls `pad` for the MAC input. Finish the two methods marked `TODO`:

items: `pad(data)`: the MAC input as the network's specification pads it;
`verify(key16, data, received)`: whether `received` is the MAC of `data`.

blocks.text: About eight lines in total. The tests compare your MACs with the network's own reference implementation.

cases.says: messages that end inside a block get the MAC the network computes, and the input is left unchanged
the right MAC verifies; a changed MAC, a changed message or a missing MAC does not
a MAC input that is already whole blocks still gets the padding block the network's method adds
a MAC shorter than 8 bytes is refused even when the bytes it has are right

origin.section: 8.6. A MAC Proves the Bytes Were Not Changed, and Hides None of Them

concepts: A MAC over the message detects any changed byte, depends on how the network pads its input, hides nothing, and is verified against all of its bytes.
